subject: Post-call: Parallel connections, burst credits & quota alignment
messages:
From: Ari Shah <ari@finledger.com>
To: tessa_morgan@redwood.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2027-04-30T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Follow-up: Parallel connections & SLO (post-call)

Thanks for the call earlier, Tessa — quick write-up from our side so we're aligned on requirements and asks before we get a formal proposal.

Summary of FinLedger requirements (from today's discovery):
- Primary API traffic: mix of short-sync calls (single-response) and streaming audit events.
- Target SLAs: P95 latency <= 250ms for sync paths, streaming end-to-end < 400ms for first-byte under typical network conditions.
- Sustained throughput: ~300 RPS (application-level requests/sec) during business hours; expected peaks up to ~1,200 RPS during batch windows.
- Concurrency profile: ~150 long-lived parallel short requests; ~200 concurrent streaming sessions that keep a socket open for 10-30 seconds on average.
- Burst behavior: unpredictable spikes up to 800–1,000 concurrent short requests for 20–60 seconds during batch starts.

Questions / asks for Redwood:
1) What connection-pool and parallel-request quotas would you recommend for a pilot?
2) Can Redwood provide temporary burst credits (or a soft quota increase) to cover 1–2 known peak events during the pilot?
3) How does Redwood handle multiplexing/keep-alive across our SDK? Any recommended settings (max idle, keep-alive timeout)?
4) Any additional telemetry you need from us (avg token length, session duration, routing breakdown) to size the pool?

I've attached a simple spreadsheet with our call-sampled concurrency traces (finledger-conn-expectations.xlsx). Please point us to the next steps and any info you need to produce a quota proposal.

Thanks — Ari
Ari Shah
Head of Platform Engineering | FinLedger
ops@finledger.com

Attachments: finledger-conn-expectations.xlsx (spreadsheet)

From: tessa_morgan@redwood.com
To: Ari Shah <ari@finledger.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2027-04-30T17:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Parallel connections & SLO (post-call)

Ari — thanks for the clear recap and the spreadsheet (very helpful). Below is a concise proposal for an initial pilot configuration and the immediate next steps we recommend.

Pilot recommendation (30-day):
- Dedicated connection pool (pilot tenant): 250 concurrent connections.
- Per-connection parallelism: allow up to 2 parallel requests per TCP connection (supporting HTTP/2 multiplexing where applicable).
- Sustained quota: 350 RPS (buffer above your 300 RPS baseline).
- Peak/burst soft-cap: enable burst window up to 1,000 concurrent short requests for up to 60 seconds (requires burst credits).
- Streaming sessions: reserve 300 concurrent streaming sessions (keeps sockets + KV cache active).
- Latency targets we aim to meet for the pilot: P95 <= 220ms (sync), first-byte streaming P95 <= 360ms.

Operational safeguards / fallbacks:
- Automatic degrade policy: if load exceeds soft-cap for > 90s, route excess requests to a lower-cost compatible model variant (configured per route).
- Telemetry we provide: per-connection occupancy, per-route token/sec, P50/P95/P99 latency, and socket churn.

Credit & billing notes:
- We can grant 48 hours of burst credits immediately to cover your first scheduled batch; additional credits for the pilot can be added upon Exec approval.
- We'll include a provisional ratecard for the pilot in the attached PDF (redwood-conn-ratecard.pdf).

Next steps (action items):
- Tessa: send a formal quota proposal (I will draft and attach).
- FinLedger: share average request payload/token lengths and a 48-hour trace export (if you can).
- Marissa: loop in Solutions Eng for a short runbook and canary checklist.

I'll attach the pilot playbook and our ratecard. If this plan looks ok, we'll follow with a HubSpot deal update and a DocuSign for the pilot terms.

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Senior Solutions Manager | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Follow-up: Parallel connections & SLO (post-call) — sizing details

On Thu, Apr 30, 2027 at 05:05 PM Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com> wrote:
> I'll attach the pilot playbook and our ratecard. If this plan looks ok, we'll follow with a HubSpot deal update and a DocuSign for the pilot terms.

Adding a few technical sizing notes from infra that will help the quota proposal be operationally correct: 
- Recommendation: reserve 250–300 connection slots, allow up to 2 concurrent request streams per connection (HTTP/2 multiplex). That gives effective parallel capacity of 500–600 concurrent inflight requests.
- Sustained throughput safety: configure token-bucket smoothing with a 60s window to absorb short spikes; this prevents immediate hard throttles for 20–60s bursts.
- Burst credits model: we support "burst tokens" that are consumed when soft-cap is exceeded; pilot can be provisioned with 50k burst tokens (equivalent to ~1,000 concurrent short requests for ~45s depending on request cost).
- Stream-specific advice: keep-alive 90s, max-idle 30s, connection reuse enabled in the SDK. If FinLedger uses long polling, enable shorter heartbeats to free sockets if idle >30s.
- Metrics we need from the customer to finalize sizing: median token-per-call, 95th-percentile session duration, and ratio of streaming vs non-streaming traffic.

Example quick config JSON (for ops):
{
  "tenant": "finledger-pilot",
  "connection_pool": 275,
  "parallel_per_conn": 2,
  "sustained_rps": 350,
  "burst_tokens": 50000,
  "stream_sessions_reserved": 300
}

I'll draft the quota proposal doc and attach it to the HubSpot record once we get the missing telemetry.

— Dev (Infra)

If you can attach the formal quota proposal and the DocuSign link we'll get legal/finance to expedite sign-off.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — Ari
